Reject all Accept all Save settings About the Node The scholarly communication layer of EOSC An e-Infrastructure Node that integrates services across the research lifecycle, so that research outputs of every discipline can be registered, published, discovered, monitored and assessed on open, European, community-governed infrastructure. Status EOSC Node, second wave Period 2026–2028 Coordinator OpenAIRE AMKE Partner OPERAS AISBL Services 15, at TRL 7–9 Overview Gap & Impact Who it serves Scope Timeline Governance On this page Overview Gap and impact Who it serves Scope Timeline Governance Contact the Node team Overview A dedicated layer within the EOSC Federation The Node is coordinated by OpenAIRE and built on its open science infrastructure, used across Europe for over fifteen years: the OpenAIRE Graph with 400M+ research records, and services for discovery, data management planning, repository onboarding, training and research monitoring and assessment. OPERAS complements it with depth in the Social Sciences and Humanities and in Diamond Open Access. All services are free at the point of use for researchers. Independent infrastructure - Compute and storage for the Node’s services are provided through OpenAIRE and OPERAS infrastructure. All services operate independently of the EOSC EU Node. Gap addressed Connecting research to its community Universities and research-performing organisations, the main producers and users of scholarly communication, remain underrepresented in the EOSC Federation. Research Infrastructures and other Nodes lack the connection to the scholarly communication ecosystem needed to monitor, discover and assess their outputs. No other Node provides this layer. Scientific impact Open scholarly communication, end to end The Node treats scholarly communication as shared, open infrastructure across the whole research lifecycle. Discovery Research from every discipline and language, findable in one connected space through the OpenAIRE Graph and GoTriple. Responsible assessment Open, transparent evidence for CoARA-aligned research assessment, beyond journal-based metrics. AI readiness Linked, openly licensed metadata built on persistent identifiers, ready for AI-driven discovery, enrichment and data-sovereign research assistants. Trust Community-governed European infrastructure with transparent provenance, reducing dependence on proprietary databases. Full lifecycle Data management planning, open publishing, interoperable repositories and research monitoring, connected end to end. Who it serves Science areas and beneficiaries All scientific disciplines Social Sciences and Humanities Meta-research Research analytics Researchers in all disciplines, with SSH depth through OPERAS Universities and RPOs: monitoring, assessment, compliance and institutional DMP tooling Research funders: policy dashboards and mandate tracking Diamond OA publishers and platforms Repository and publishing platform managers National and thematic EOSC Nodes The scientometrics and meta-research community Policymakers Scope Three objectives for the build-up phase 01 A joint scholarly communication offer Integrate the Node’s services with the EOSC Federated AAI, register them in the EOSC Catalogue, and deliver three multi-Node use cases. 02 Onboarding more services Bring further open European services into the Federation, and act as a forum on interoperability, policy and sustainability. 03 Rules, business models and governance Shape how the Federation’s rules and business models apply to services that are open by nature and community-governed. Timeline Six milestones, September 2026 to August 2028 M1 Sep 2026 Node kick-off; project work plan and OpenAIRE–OPERAS partnership agreement finalised. M6 Feb 2027 All TRL 9 services registered in the EOSC Catalogue; Node charter drafted. M9 May 2027 EOSC Federated AAI integration roadmap complete; user and API documentation published; third-party onboarding template available; second batch of TRL 7–8 services registered. M12 Aug 2027 Rules of participation report; service packages defined; UC1 prototype; OpenPlato training modules. M18 Feb 2028 All three use cases operational; business model, sustainability and governance reports; updated documentation. M24 Aug 2028 Node operations report, lessons learned, and contributions to the EOSC Federation Handbook. Timeline Coordinated by OpenAIRE, with OPERAS as partner As more services join, contributing partners take a larger role in decisions, moving the Node towards broader, community-governed operation. Quarterly Node Steering Board OpenAIRE and OPERAS leadership. Sets strategic direction and oversees the partnership and alignment with EOSC Federation governance. Bi-monthly Node Operations Committee Node officers and technical leads. Runs day-to-day operations, service integration and use case delivery. At key milestones - tbc. Advisory Group The NOAD network, OPERAS members, National Nodes and external stakeholders. Advises on service design and onboarding priorities.

Each service in the Node is operated by OpenAIRE AMKE or OPERAS AISBL, under that organisation's own policies. Node-level policies are being adopted during the build-up phase. Overview Gap & Impact Who it serves Scope Timeline Governance On this page Overview Policies in force Personal data Security Liability and access Acceptable Use Policy User Access Policy Contact Points Questions Overview Every service in the Node operates under the policies of the organisation that runs it. These policies are in force now, and they are the documents to read before using a service. This page also sets out the Node's Acceptable Use Policy and User Access Policy, and who to contact about terms, personal data and security. Policies that apply today Operator Policy Applies to OpenAIRE AMKE Terms and Conditions of Service OpenAIRE Graph, Scholexplorer, EXPLORE, CONNECT, PROVIDE, MONITOR, UsageCounts, Argos, MyResearchFolio Privacy Policy and the Personal Data Protection Policy for OpenAIRE Services All OpenAIRE services Acceptable Use Policy OpenAIRE infrastructure and APIs All OpenAIRE policies Index of everything above, plus service-specific policies OPERAS AISBL Terms of Use GoTriple, VERA, OPERAS Metrics, Pathfinder Privacy Policy All OPERAS services Personal data Under the EOSC Federation Framework Agreement (Article 9.1), each organisation remains solely responsible for its own compliance with data protection law, including deciding whether it acts as controller or processor for a given service. The Node does not act as a single controller for all its services. For any question about your personal data, contact the operator of the service you used, OpenAIRE AMKE or OPERAS AISBL, using the contacts in their privacy policies. Services that handle researcher identifiers, including MyResearchFolio, Argos and OpenCDMP, operate under a GDPR-compliant data protection framework. Data protection impact assessments are maintained for the relevant services and reviewed every year, under the oversight of the Node Legal Officer. Security Node services are hosted in certified data centres and operate under the established security policies and incident response procedures of their operators. The Node has a designated Cybersecurity Officer. Security incidents that materially affect the EOSC Federation are notified to the EOSC Association and the Federation's operational committee without undue delay, in accordance with Article 9A.3 of the Framework Agreement. To report a security issue in a Node service, contact the operator of that service directly. The operator notifies the Node Cybersecurity Officer. Liability and Access Services are provided free at the point of use to researchers, on the terms of the operating organisation. Liability for the provision and use of an individual service is governed by that service's own terms, not by this page and not by the Federation-level agreement. Bulk data from the OpenAIRE Graph is available under open licences, including CC BY, and the APIs are open. Access conditions differ by service and are stated for each service in its EOSC Catalogue entry and on the Node services page. Acceptable Use Policy and Conditions of Use Version 1.0 · 19 October 2026 Introduction This Acceptable Use Policy and Conditions of Use ("AUP") sets the rules and conditions for your access to and use (including transmission, processing and storage of data) of the resources and services ("Services") offered through the EOSC Scholarly Commons Node, for the purpose of supporting open scholarly communication and research in the European Open Science Cloud. Each Service is operated by OpenAIRE AMKE or OPERAS AISBL (the "Operators"), as indicated on the page of the Service. By accessing or using the Services, you accept this AUP. Conditions You shall use the Services only in a way consistent with the purposes and limitations described above, show consideration towards other users, avoid causing harm to the Services and cooperate in resolving issues arising from your use. You shall use the Services only for lawful purposes and shall not breach, attempt to breach or circumvent administrative or security controls. You shall not interfere with the normal operation of the Services, including by exceeding published rate limits. You shall respect intellectual property rights, licence conditions and confidentiality agreements. You shall protect your access credentials (for example passwords, private keys or multi-factor tokens); no intentional sharing is permitted. You shall keep your registration information correct and up to date. You shall promptly report known or suspected security breaches, credential compromise or misuse to the security contact below, and report compromised credentials to the issuing authority. You may rely on the Services only to the extent set out in any applicable service level agreement with the Operator. Use without such an agreement is at your own risk, to the extent permitted by applicable law. Your personal data will be processed in accordance with the privacy notices referenced below. Your use of the Services may be restricted or suspended where necessary for administrative, operational or security reasons, without prior notice and without compensation. If you violate these rules, you may be liable for the consequences, which may include suspension of your account and a report to your home organisation or to the competent authorities. children.main_text: Services for the scholarly commons . 7 services from trusted providers, for institutions, funders, research teams and individual researchers. Start from a task, or filter your way in. Search I want to… Plan my data DMP templates, funder requirements, machine-actionable output Publish & preserve Repositories with DOIs, versioning and long-term custody Work with metadata Graph dumps, citation data, APIs and SPARQL endpoints Monitor open science Dashboards and indicators for projects, institutions, countries All services 7 results Show All Open to anyone Set up for your organisation Open Access Argos Plan your data management: Create, link and share Data Management Plans Develop and publish your Data Management Plan on the cloud. Manage Data Researchers, Research Projects, Research Communities, Research Organisations, Funders, Businesses Openaire Details Order required OpenAIRE CONNECT Custom Gateway for your Community OpenAIRE CONNECT is a platform‑as‑a‑service that empowers research communities to create and manage customised Community Gateways. Discover Research Communities, Research Infrastructure Managers, Research Projects, Research Organisations Openaire Details Open Access OpenAIRE Graph An intelligent gateway to scholarly communication The OpenAIRE Graph is a collection of interlinked research objects that aggregates metadata records from more than 70K scholarly communication sources from all over the world for researchers, service providers, research managers and policy makers, by following a participatory approach. Discover Providers, Research Communities, Research Groups, Research Infrastructure Managers, Research Managers, Research Organisations, Innovators, Businesses, Provider Managers Openaire Details Open Access OpenAIRE MONITOR Personalised research monitoring OpenAIRE MONITOR is a service that produces well-documented, timely and accurate monitoring indicators of research activities for funders, research initiatives and organisations, by creating personalised and on-demand online configurable dashboards. Assess Funders, Research Infrastructure Managers, Research Organisations Openaire Details Open Access OpenAIRE PROVIDE One-stop-shop for sharing, improving, and enriching your content OpenAIRE PROVIDE is the scholarly gateway that receives content registration requests and provides guidance for content providers by viewing a personalised, user-friendly dashboard that shows the necessary steps and status of the services to complete the process. Outreach Providers, Provider Managers Openaire Details Open Access OpenAIRE UsageCounts Measure.Track Open Access repositories usage UsageCounts is an OpenAIRE service for content providers, research funders and policy makers, that collects and visualises usage activity of Open Access Repositories by using automated and standardised scientific methods. OpenPlato is a modular learning platform developed by OpenAIRE to support training in Open Science, Research Data Management, and related topics across Europe.
